item.title: Living longer could hinge on one surprising dietary change, study review suggests
item.description: A review of 350+ studies finds protein restriction triggers the hormone FGF21, delivering longevity benefits similar to calorie restriction.
item.content:encoded:
Eating less protein, not cutting calories, may be an easier path to a longer, healthier life for sedentary adults, according to a new scientific review.

While previous research has long tied calorie restriction to improved lifespan and lower rates of age-related disease, studies have found that many people have difficulty maintaining strict low-calorie diets.

A review of more than 350 studies published in the journal Cell Press Blue suggests that targeted protein restriction can deliver similar metabolic benefits without the need to cut calories.

LEADING ONCOLOGIST REVEALS 6 HABITS THAT COULD PROMOTE LONGEVITY AND REDUCE YOUR RISK OF CHRONIC ILLNESS

Across the reviewed studies, lower protein intake was associated with better metabolism, altered nutrient signaling, reduced cellular damage and improved cellular maintenance, according to the published review.

Much of the benefit stems from a metabolic hormone known as fibroblast growth factor 21, or FGF21. Restricting protein triggers a surge in FGF21, which animal studies have shown can boost energy expenditure, reduce inflammation, improve blood sugar control and extend lifespan.

Researchers highlighted three essential amino acids that are building blocks of protein — methionine, isoleucine and valine. Under certain conditions, they may contribute to biological pathways associated with aging under certain conditions.

FORGET THE GYM: A 30-SECOND TEST MAY BE ONE OF THE BEST INDICATORS OF LONGEVITY

For people who don't exercise regularly, high levels of these amino acids may keep certain growth-related processes constantly active. Over time, that stimulation can create cellular damage, systemic inflammation and weight gain.

"It's absolutely crystal-clear that there are benefits of protein for muscle growth and exercise response of active individuals," said Dudley Lamming, the paper’s corresponding author and a researcher at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

"But because most people are relatively sedentary, many people are likely consuming more protein than they actually need, which probably has negative health consequences," he added in the press release.

There were some limitations to the study findings. Because the paper is a scientific review rather than a new clinical trial, it identifies patterns across existing research but cannot establish cause and effect in humans, the researchers acknowledged.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Longer-term human studies are still needed to determine whether these metabolic benefits ultimately translate into increased lifespan, they noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The review emphasizes that protein needs are not one-size-fits-all, and that the findings should not be interpreted as a recommendation to consume inadequate amounts.

Physically active people and athletes process protein differently. Exercise helps to direct dietary amino acids toward building and repairing muscle instead of leaving excess amino acids to be processed by the body, the researchers noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

High protein intake is also crucial for pregnant women and older adults who may face age-related muscle loss.

For the broader, largely inactive population, the findings suggest that public health guidelines should move away from sweeping recommendations and instead tailor protein targets to a person's age and activity level.

item.title: Raiders franchise that once embraced an outlaw image now has 'no turds,' coach Klint Kubiak says
item.description: Coach Klint Kubiak says the Las Vegas Raiders don't have "any turds," marking a stark departure from the franchise's storied outlaw history.
item.content:encoded:
It's a new day for the Las Vegas Raiders, and by that we're talking about a time with a new head coach, new coaching staff, new veteran players and new rookies starting with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

It's also apparently the time for a new disposition and personality around the storied franchise.

"I think we just have a professional group of players, you know?" coach Klint Kubiak told reporters on Monday. "They care about getting better."

TOM BRADY GIVES RAIDERS HARSH 'REALITY' CHECK AFTER THE TEAM WON ONLY THREE GAMES IN 2025

And this:

"We don't have any turds," Kubiak pointed out. "We got guys that want to be here. that want to win, that want to change this place. I'm really, really happy with that."

This is good. It's often good when a football team has no, using Kubiak's word, "turds."

But aside from it being a good thing, it's kind of a different thing for the Raiders.

There was a time, you see, mostly starting in the rollicking 1960s, through the rocking 1970s, and probably all the way through to the early 2000s, when the Raiders had some, shall we say, questionable guys.

They were a team that boasted a roster with renegades. And owner Al Davis, who once sued the NFL and moved the franchise multiple times to the chagrin of his fellow owners, embraced the outlaw image.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

This is a franchise that had a starting safety named Jack Tatum. His playing style led to him being nicknamed "The Assassin," which made him quite polarizing, especially after one of his hits left receiver Darryl Stingley paralyzed.

"I like to believe that my best hits border on felonious assault," Tatum wrote in his autobiography.

This franchise didn't draft John Matuszak, but Davis found the boundary-pushing, difficult-to-coach individualist a perfect fit for the Raiders.

Matuszak struggled with alcohol and drug use throughout and after his playing career. In his autobiography, he openly admitted using prescription painkillers, cocaine and steroids while in the NFL.

And yet he was a key defensive lineman on Oakland's Super Bowl XI and Super Bowl XV champions.

There were others, of course.

Warren Wells was one of the AFL's most explosive wide receivers in the mid-to-late 1960s — until his career was derailed by a rape conviction that sent him to prison.

Even the team's The Autumn Wind anthem — adopted from an NFL Films feature on the Raiders — is an embrace of the franchise's outlaw reputation.

The Autumn Wind is a Raider,

Pillaging just for fun.

He'll knock you 'round and upside down,

And laugh when he's conquered and won."

For the record, the Raiders of this century have not enjoyed anything close to the success those teams of yesteryear authored. But the latter-day Raiders also had, Kubiak vocabulary here, turds.

Cornerback Damon Arnette lasted only two seasons with the club until weapons and drug-related charges made him impossible to keep. The former first-round pick, bouncing around the NFL and other leagues, is a free agent.

Henry Ruggs III wasn't a "turd" in the classic sense of the NFL meaning. But he made tragic decisions that led him to drive drunk, killing a woman and her dog in a fiery crash years ago.

There are also more recent players such as Charles Snowden and Rodric Teamer who were arrested on charges of DUI, significant enough that the Raiders quickly cut them.

And there was Chandler Jones, who was arrested multiple times in 2023 on charges of violating domestic violence protective orders. Jones was eventually placed on the non-football illness list for what club sources described as "concerning" behavior.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But this Raiders team is apparently different.

Born-again Christian Kirk Cousins is the presumptive starting quarterback. Mendoza has such a polished public personality it borders on implausible. Maxx Crosby is one aggressive dude on the field, but off the field those videos of him and his little girl will melt your heart.

These Raiders apparently don't have the image of those fateful Autumn Wind clubs. And Klint Kubiak likes it.

item.title: ‘Doctor’ El-Sayed’s bizarre health hustle raises campaign headache: ‘Moon Juice Brain Dust’
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed criticized Mehmet Oz for selling health products as a doctor, then used his own medical credentials to promote supplements and devices.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed made money promoting health products, including while invoking his medical credentials, despite saying he broadly rejected advertisements for products making health claims and criticizing others for doing the same.

Before running for Senate, El-Sayed hosted a podcast that provided him with a six-figure income partially through ad reads. Among the companies El-Sayed promoted for cash, often citing his purported experience as a doctor, were firms selling supplements, peptides, and an Israeli metabolism-tracking device that has been scrutinized by health experts.

The ad reads came despite an assurance from El-Sayed that he would not use his platform to sell health products to people who listen to him.

SOCIALISM'S WAR ON SUCCESS HAS A NEW CHAMPION — AND HE’S RUNNING FOR SENATE IN MICHIGAN

"I broadly reject any advertisements that are for products making claims about health," he wrote in a now-deleted social media post from March 2022.

El-Sayed also accused Mehmet Oz during his 2022 Pennsylvania Senate run of being part of the "medical industrial complex that exists to sell you things that you don’t need that are not actually based in any level of science."

"Yet he can … say, ‘Well, I’m a doctor, so you should trust what I have to say,'" El-Sayed added.

DR OZ REVEALS THE HEALTHY RETIREMENT HABIT THAT COULD MAKE AMERICA $1 TRILLION RICHER

After assuring his audience that he wouldn't hawk health products, and criticizing Oz for using his medical credentials for doing so, El-Sayed used his medical credentials to sell health products.

"Even as a doctor and epidemiologist, nutrition labels are obnoxiously hard to process," El-Sayed said during a March 2025 ad read. "That's where Thrive Market comes in. See, I love Thrive Market, my go to online grocery store for getting all of my healthy essentials delivered. And I don't even have to leave my couch."

Thrive Market has sold a wide selection of supplements, including items such as "Moon Juice Brain Dust" and "Royal Jelly Brain Fuel" that claim to improve the cognitive function of those who use them. Health experts have cast doubt on whether or not such supplements can actually improve brain function.

Moon Juice Brain Dust describes itself as a "nootropic blend of adaptogens and herbs that target stress to support mental stamina, alertness, and concentration" that is "informed by Traditional Chinese Medicine and Ayurveda." Royal jelly, meanwhile, is a thick, milky substance produced by bees to feed their queen. Proponents argue it can be helpful in treating menopause symptoms or addressing low energy, though scientific evidence for such claims is limited.

Thrive did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

IV THERAPY AND SUPPLEMENTS UNDER SCRUTINY AS EXPERTS WARN OF POTENTIAL SIDE EFFECTS

While El-Sayed has leaned heavily on his identity as a doctor both in doing ad reads and on the campaign trail, public records indicate that he never held a medical license or completed a residency. He does, however, hold a medical degree and a doctorate degree in public health.

The New York Post was the first to report on El-Sayed’s advertisement for health goods.

A company making moon dust and brain jelly wasn’t El-Sayed’s only customer.

On July 23, 2024, El-Sayed read an ad promoting a medical device created by an Israel-based startup. 

"Lumen is the world's first handheld metabolic coach. It's a device that measures your metabolism through your breath and on the app. It lets you know if you're burning fat or carbs and gives you tailored guidance to improve your nutrition, workout, sleep, and even manage your stress," he said. "All you've got to do is breathe into your Lumen first thing in the morning, and it'll give you an inside look into what's going on with your metabolism, whether you're burning mostly fats or carbs."

Years before El-Sayed took Lumen’s advertising money, experts were raising concerns about its medical claims.

"I just don’t see a practical use for the product in helping people achieve their weight-loss goals," Harbor-UCLA Medical Center senior researcher Nicholas Tiller told Outside Magazine in 2022. "The use of metabolic flexibility and other science-sounding terms lend the product a false scientific legitimacy."

"It’s quintessential marketing over science," he added.

El-Sayed also advertised for a company offering a peptide that allegedly improves skin health.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

item.title: Mamdani's grocery giveaway hits ID snag as critics cry foul: 'Make it make sense'
item.description: A cabinet official's mention of a "library card-esque system" for NYC's government-run grocery stores sparked fierce voter ID hypocrisy accusations.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s game plan for government-run grocery stores faced criticism Monday after a city official told reporters a "library-card-esque system" may be employed to prevent abuse of the 30% discounted markets.

Mamdani took a question from a reporter who asked about preventing bulk purchases of groceries at the artificial discount from being re-sold at MSRP or higher.

The mayor responded that the government grocery Request-for-Proposal makes clear "this is a program for New Yorkers to be able to put food on the table, not a program for people to be able to make a quick buck through reselling. I'm going to pass it over to our EDC head, Jeanny Pak, to add some additional details."

MAMDANI’S CITY GROCERY PLAN COULD LEAVE TAXPAYERS PAYING FOR EVERY BANANA

It was Pak’s follow-up that raised eyebrows, given Mamdani and many Democrats’ staunch opposition to voter ID and Republicans’ SAVE America Act moving through Congress.

"[W]e are looking to make sure that we target New Yorkers, whether it be a sort of a library card-esque thing, and also we manage who's buying and that is focused on everyday New Yorkers," Pak said.

"So, we are mindful of that, and so we're going to make sure that we have all the things in place to ensure that that does not happen."

SEN MARK WARNER CALLED OUT IN ABC INTERVIEW FOR INACCURATE VOTER ID CLAIMS

When asked about the apparent divergence between Pak’s response referencing a possible ID card-type system and opposition to voter ID, a Mamdani spokesperson said it was an apples-to-oranges contrast.

"Comparisons to voter ID laws or the SAVE Act simply do not apply. This is not an identification system, nor is it a mechanism to verify who someone is, where they live, or how much they earn," Mamdani’s spokesperson said.

"It is a practical inventory management tool to ensure affordable groceries remain available for the people who need them instead of being cleared off shelves for resale."

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

The spokesperson pointed to the mayor’s comments specifically regarding bulk-buying concerns, saying that was the premise of the reporter’s question — not whether people from Pennsylvania, New Jersey or upstate New York would be able to shop at the subsidized outlets.

"To be absolutely clear: NYC Grocery stores will be open to everyone," the spokesperson said.

"There will be no system to verify identity, residency, or income, and no one will be asked to show ID to shop."

Instead of an "ID," the spokesperson said the stores may employ a "customer card" similar to loyalty programs at other grocers like ShopRite, Food Lion or Weis.

The "customer card" would be designed by the "private operator" of the city-run store to "help manage supply and prevent people from buying large quantities of discounted staples for resale" and is strictly intended to "make sure the savings reach families putting food on the table."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Customers will not need to apply through City Hall or any agency, the spokesperson added.

Critics were unconvinced.

"ID for government cheese," said Philadelphia radio host Rich Zeoli.

"After all, we have to make sure no one crosses the border and if they do, the police will be called. So it's good to see Mamdani now supports ID (just not for voting), border control, and law enforcement," Zeoli tweeted.

Former Texas congressional candidate Nick Plumb commented on X that "Mamdani wants to protect taxpayer funded grocery store[s] from non-NYC residents they’ll need an ID card to enter. You can[t] make this up."

Former Virginia Attorney General Jason Miyares, a supporter of voter ID who also opposed the Old Dominion’s recent failed attempt to redraw congressional lines to Democrats’ advantage, also criticized the mayor.

"So let me get this straight: Taxpayer-funded grocery store? Better show a valid ID or you can’t buy milk," Miyares said.

"Voting for the people who decide how those taxes get spent? A valid ID is somehow ‘racist’ and ‘oppressive’. Unbelievable," he said.

When asked whether the mayor's office believed the loyalty card system constituted a form of identification, a Mamdani spokesperson directed Fox News Digital to a paragraph in the Request for Proposal (RFP) that prospective store operators must follow:

"The Operator(s) will create a voluntary free-to-access membership card program to monitor sales activity, and implement the discount program and any associated demand management measures. The savings card shall not be required for physical access to N.Y.C. Groceries site(s) and shall be made easily available to any individual requesting one," the section read.

"Make it make sense," added FOX News host Sean Hannity.

New York Republican Congresswoman Claudia Tenney added: "So ID for government grocery stores to stop people abusing the system is fine, but requiring ID to vote not? Got it."

SAVE Act supporter Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., added on X that the hypocrisy must "stop."

"Democrats: Are fighting to ensure you don’t have to show an ID before voting in our elections. Also Democrats: Want you to show an ID before entering a supermarket."

"Oh, the irony is too much," said X CEO Elon Musk.

item.title: Moscow bombing exposes potential security gaps around Putin’s military elite, expert says
item.description: An analyst warns Putin’s effort to project normalcy may have left Moscow exposed after a fatal restaurant bombing reportedly targeted a senior Russian general at a private celebration.
item.content:encoded:
Russian President Vladimir Putin's drive to project "normalcy" in Moscow may have created a dangerous security blind spot, giving adversaries like Ukraine greater opportunities to target the Kremlin's military elite, an analyst said Monday.

The assessment came after a deadly explosion ripped through an upscale Moscow restaurant on Aug. 1, where a senior Russian general was reportedly attending a private celebration. Several Russian media outlets claimed the bombing targeted Col. Gen. Alexander Chaiko, who led the troops that made a botched attempt to storm the Ukrainian capital in 2022 and recently was appointed the chief of Russia’s aerospace forces. The claims could not be independently verified.

If Chaiko was indeed at the restaurant, "that would establish a compelling motive for Ukraine," Dr. Mark Episkopos, a Eurasia research fellow at the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, told Fox News Digital. "But there has been an ongoing discourse inside Russia that, despite numerous such attacks, Russian elites and even military figures continue to flout [operational security] best practices by holding parties like this in the first place."

The Russian Embassy in Rome accused Kyiv of carrying out the attack and said in a statement Aug. 2 that the attack was "evidence that the Ukrainian terrorist contagion is already beginning to spread."

MAYOR CALLS UPSCALE RESTAURANT BOMBING A 'BRUTAL TERRORIST ACT'

"The other factor here is that Putin has done his best to preserve a sense of ‘normalcy’ in Moscow and St. Petersburg, cultivating a facade of stability that Ukraine has been able to exploit," Episkopos added.

Russia’s National Anti-Terrorism Committee said an unidentified woman carried an improvised explosive device to the Balzi Rossi restaurant. The committee said the woman was stopped by security before the bomb was detonated near the restaurant's entrance. The Russian Embassy in Rome on Monday said five people were killed and 19 were injured in the attack.

UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

"This particular event did seem to have a substantial level of security, which is why the person carrying the explosive was reportedly stopped and questioned at the entrance," Episkopos noted.

Russian investigators suggested the courier may not have known she was transporting explosives and said the device was detonated remotely.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin condemned the "brutal terrorist attack," vowing that those responsible would be punished, according to Deutsche Welle.

'A NEW KIND OF WAR': INSIDE UKRAINE'S HIDDEN FACTORIES MASS-PRODUCING COMBAT DRONES

"The means by which this attack was executed — a remotely detonated explosive device delivered on-site by a civilian — are also consistent with other assassinations deep inside Russian territory previously attributed to Ukraine," Episkopos said.

"These include those of Lt. Gen. Igor Kirillov, Lt. Gen. Yaroslav Moskalik, Lt. Gen. Fanil Sarvarov, pro-Kremlin blogger Vladlen Tatarsky and others," he said.

Ukraine had not publicly commented on the restaurant bombing as of Monday afternoon, and no group had claimed responsibility.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow has repeatedly accused Kyiv of targeting senior military officers, pro-war figures and Russian-installed officials.

MOSCOW, TALIBAN FORGE MILITARY ALLIANCE IN POWER GRAB AFTER US AFGHANISTAN EXIT: REPORTS

Episkopos noted that Kyiv has increasingly used unconventional tactics to offset Russia's superiority in conventional manpower and firepower.

"Ukraine has pioneered a new style of asymmetric warfare that plays to its strengths and Russia's weaknesses — relatively porous borders and vast territory that's difficult to monitor, let alone defend," he said. "Ukraine's interior is smaller and comparatively better controlled, and the intelligence it receives from Western partners plays a role here."

NATO MEMBER SCRAMBLES FIGHTER JETS AS RUSSIAN ATTACK ON UKRAINE KILLS 8

Episkopos added: "This makes operations like this more difficult to pull off. Russia has generally relied on its advantage in raw firepower to conduct airstrikes, as opposed to covert assassinations, against high-value Ukrainian targets."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Scott Eastwood told Shia LaBeouf 'I'm going to whoop your a--' during tense on-set clash
item.description: Scott Eastwood detailed the confrontation with Shia LaBeouf, reflected on the actor's intense approach to acting and criticized another unnamed actor who he claims quit a film mid-production.
item.content:encoded:
Scott Eastwood has a bone to pick with Shia LaBeouf. 

During an appearance on Dax Shepard’s "Armchair Expert" podcast, the actor, 40, opened up about a "tense" on-set moment during the filming of the 2014 film, "Fury," in which he nearly got into a physical altercation with the former Disney star. 

"There was sort of an incident that happened," Eastwood, 40, said. "I’ve talked about it. Brad Pitt sort of broke up a little, a tense moment."

Eastwood explained that LaBeouf — who played tank gunner Boyd "Bible" Swan in the World War ll movie — was a "very method" actor, who pulled out his tooth and cut himself at one point. 

"And I remember thinking, ‘OK, this guy’s crazy. I’m just going to keep clear from this guy.’ I don’t play this game. You go and do that, but there’s plenty of ways to do a performance in a movie and be professional also, right?"

Eastwood claimed that LaBeouf wasn't impressed with his decision of "spitting tobacco on the tank," an action that was written in the script. 

"And then finally, I just said, ‘Enough’s enough.’ I said, ‘Hey, f--- you.’ I said, ‘Stop pulling your s---.’ I said, ‘I’m going to whoop your a--,’" he continued. "And then, you know, he got … And then everyone broke it up."

This isn't the first time Eastwood has called out a Hollywood actor. 

During a recent appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience" podcast, Eastwood recalled working with an unnamed celebrity who abruptly walked away from a film after production was already underway, leaving the cast and crew left scrambling.

"Without saying any names ... people get too famous for too long. They think the world owes them something," Eastwood said.

CLINT EASTWOOD'S SON SHARES UPDATE ON 94-YEAR-OLD DAD MONTHS AFTER LONGTIME PARTNER'S DEATH

According to the "Lucky Strike" actor, the actor decided they no longer wanted to work with another person involved in the project after a significant amount of money had already been spent.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"They decided after we'd already spent a bunch of money that they just didn't want to work with this other person and didn't want to do the job," Eastwood claimed. "I was like, 'You need to pay that money back to the person who invested in you.' And they said, 'I'm not going to do that.'"

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Instead, Eastwood claimed the actor simply left the project — despite it being centered on "their story."

'MOBLAND' STAR TOM HARDY ACCUSED OF 'CAREER SUICIDE' AFTER ALLEGEDLY LEAVING CASTMATES STRANDED ON SET: REPORT

"It's black and white. Do the right thing. Don't be a piece of s—. You can't do that," Eastwood said, calling the situation "shocking" and "unbelievable."

The son of Oscar-winning filmmaker Clint Eastwood said the incident left him reflecting on a bigger issue looming within Hollywood.

SCOTT EASTWOOD CREDITS HIS FAMOUS FATHER'S WORK ETHIC FOR MAKING HIM AWARE OF 'BULLS---' IN THE FILM INDUSTRY

"I've seen some behavior in this business that is shocking," Eastwood said. "That would not go in other industries, but for some reason because we idolize [actors]..."

Despite the negative experience, Eastwood said he still very much enjoys what he does.

"I love telling stories," he said.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers eviscerates Anthony Fauci after pleading the Fifth at Senate hearing: 'Absolute criminal'
item.description: Aaron Rodgers called Anthony Fauci an "absolute coward" for pleading the Fifth 111 times at a Senate hearing, then turned his fire on ESPN too.
item.content:encoded:
A simple question from Pat McAfee led Pittsburgh Steelers four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers to unload on Dr. Anthony Fauci, mocking the former Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for recently invoking the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing this past week.

"Can you tell us about your mindset coming into your last season?" McAfee asked.

The ESPN personality couldn’t have guessed where the four-time NFL MVP was about to take this.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I’m gonna plead the Fifth," Rodgers said, as McAfee and the Steelers fans watching at training camp laughed in unison, "like that absolute coward Tony Fauci. Absolute coward. Are you kidding me? You get a pardon and you’re and you pleaded over 100 times at the White House? What are you scared of, Tony? I thought you were the science. ‘I am science,’ and you get up there and can’t answer a question? What are we doing?"

Rodgers is referencing an infamous remark by Fauci during a 2021 interview, where he defended his public health policies during the COVID-19 pandemic, saying "I am the science."

PAT MCAFEE POKES FUN AT ANTHONY FAUCI PLEADING THE FIFTH AMENDMENT LIVE ON ESPN

Fauci pled the Fifth 111 times during a Senate hearing, on the advice of his attorneys, to answer questions from the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, chaired by Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky. He was questioned over his response to the pandemic and his policy decisions, where the former White House COVID advisor was accused of funding gain-of-function research in Wuhan, China.

Paul argued Fauci using the Fifth Amendment was unsupported because former President Joe Biden, whom Fauci advised during the pandemic, pardoned him. Paul said the committee will vote this week on a resolution to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress.

"Spending the entire time writing in his diary about how fun it is to be famous. You gotta be kidding me," Rodgers’ diatribe continued. "What are you going to say about me now? Seriously, what are they going to say about me now? Now, you can’t talk about the COVID stuff because obviously it was made in a lab in China. That’s like not even questionable anymore. Tony Fauci is an absolute criminal.

"It’s been a great life and a great career, and it’s nice to be sitting on this side now especially after that coward pled the Fifth over 100 times. I thought you had a pardon there, Tony. Why couldn’t you answer one question the entire time?"

But Rodgers wasn’t just airing out his grievances with Fauci, which he's had many since the days of the pandemic. He pointed the finger directly at the network he was being interviewed on.

No matter how McAfee and his supporting cast tried to get the conversation back on track, Rodgers took aim at ESPN, the sports network giant which airs "The Pat McAfee Show" daily.

Rodgers was vilified for his own 2021 COVID saga, where his "immunized" remark in August, months prior to testing positive for COVID-19 in November of that season, led to immediate backlash in the media.

SEN RAND PAUL QUESTIONS WHETHER FAUCI'S INVOKING THE FIFTH AMENDMENT WAS VALID AFTER BIDEN PARDON

"How much time did the network spend on that? How much time did they spend on my responses every week? On my vaccination status? On Taylor’s [Swift] and Travis’ [Kelce] wedding? Did they do even a minute on Tony Fauci? No, I bet they didn’t," Rodgers said on Monday.

Rodgers even brought up the Dianna Russini scandal and the lack of coverage from ESPN with it. Russini, who worked for ESPN before joining The Athletic, was entrenched in a scandal as an inappropriate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was exposed this offseason, ultimately leading to her exit from The Athletic and Vrabel leaving the Patriots during the NFL Draft to enter counseling.

In 2021, Rodgers was asked by reporters if he was vaccinated, to which the then-Green Bay Packers signal caller said he was "immunized". He later sought an appeal from the NFL and the NFLPA to treat his alternative antibody treatment as equivalent to being vaccinated for COVID-19. The league denied it.

Rodgers was officially classified an unvaccinated player, and then he tested positive for COVID-19 on Nov. 3, 2021, leading to a mandatory 10-day quarantine period that forced him to miss a game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Two days later, he used McAfee’s show to explain his stance, stating he had an allergy to an ingredient in mRNA vaccines, and explained his alternative treatment. Rodgers later admitted on another episode of the show that he "misled people" by calling himself immunized, though he doubled down that he did not lie.

Now, Fauci’s refusal to answer has Rodgers going full tilt years after dealing with constant scrutiny, whether it’s the man himself or the network he has issues with. Rodgers has never shied away from sharing his feelings about certain individuals, media networks, or anything in between.

And after reconciling with his family – Rodgers, his parents, and brother Luke have patched things up after a decade-long estrangement – he asks the question.

"What are you going to say now?" Rodgers said into the ESPN camera lenses.

This season marks 22 years Rodgers has starred in the NFL, and he doubled down recently saying this will be his final year.

item.title: Trump administration's immigration push fuels ICE's biggest arrest month in agency history
item.description: ICE averaged roughly 1,645 immigration arrests per day in July, smashing June's record of 43,000 as new funding and personnel fuel the crackdown.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration's immigration crackdown reached a historic milestone in July as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement made roughly 51,000 immigration arrests, setting the highest monthly arrest total in the agency's history.

ICE averaged approximately 1,645 immigration arrests per day during the month, according to multiple federal sources who spoke with Fox News.

The historic total came just one month after ICE set what was then a new monthly record with roughly 43,000 arrests in June, giving the agency back-to-back record-breaking months.

TRUMP DHS CHIEF UNDER FIRE FROM CONSERVATIVES AFTER IMMIGRATION SPEECH IGNITES BACKLASH

Federal sources told Fox News the surge followed a slowdown in ICE arrests in the weeks and months after unrest in Minneapolis.

They attributed the record-setting pace to the end of the Department of Homeland Security shutdown, thousands of newly hired ICE personnel hitting the streets and billions of dollars in new funding from two reconciliation bills that replenished the agency's coffers.

The additional money is helping fuel expanded hiring and enforcement operations nationwide, according to the sources.

ICE NABS ILLEGAL ALIENS CONVICTED OF CHILD SEX CRIMES AND METH TRAFFICKING IN NATIONWIDE ENFORCEMENT SWEEP

item.title: Notre Dame caves, lives up to Marcus Freeman's promise as USC rivalry game is officially back
item.description: Notre Dame caved to USC's scheduling demands, agreeing to play their rivalry game early in the season starting in 2030 at the LA Memorial Coliseum.
item.content:encoded:
One of college football's best rivalries is officially back.

The annual "Greatest intersectional rivalry" game between the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and USC Trojans was supposed to return to Los Angeles in 2026 after the two teams played in South Bend in 2025. But the two sides could not come to an agreement on when the game should be played, with USC wanting to move the game earlier in the season to accommodate their Big Ten Conference schedule. Notre Dame, meanwhile, wanted to leave it where it's traditionally been played: October in Indiana and November in LA.

Notre Dame, though, has no conference schedule to worry about, no potential conference championship game to consider. They set their own schedules, with a handful of games against ACC opponents their only obligation. Their special arrangement with the College Football Playoff, where simply getting to the Top 12 guarantees them a spot, despite the easier road they have, gives them yet another advantage.

ILLINOIS COACH BRET BIELEMA FIRES BACK AT NOTRE DAME AD OVER RECENT REMARKS: 'JUST JOIN A CONFERENCE'

Head coach Marcus Freeman also specifically addressed scheduling concerns, saying he'd play the game at any point in the season because it's good for the sport.

"It’s pretty black and white for me," Freeman said in 2025, per BlueAndGold.com. "You want my opinion? I want to play them every single year. When? I don’t care. I don’t care when we play them. Start of the season, middle of the season, end of the season — I don’t care. I want to play USC every year because it’s great for college football."

But when push came to shove, the Irish balked at moving the game earlier in the season, preferring instead to set up a remarkably, uh, generous schedule for themselves in 2026. USC walked away, leading head coach Lincoln Riley to repeatedly bring up that Freeman and the Irish had not lived up to their statements. The rivalry game was canceled, a disappointing end to one of the most highly anticipated games on the national college football calendar, not to mention for the fanbases of both schools.

Well, Monday morning brought welcome news: the Irish caved.

Notre Dame and USC both announced the return of the rivalry game, though not until the 2030 season. And sure enough, the game, at least for the four years of the new agreement, will be played early in the season, precisely as USC wanted.

"USC's historic rivalry with Notre Dame holds a special place in the history of college football, and we are happy to resume a series that means so much to the entire Trojan Family," said SC athletic director Jen Cohen in a statement. "It remains important for us to play this game early in the season, as it allows us to schedule competitively with our Big Ten peers and takes into account the health and best interests of our student-athletes and program. We are excited for our fans, and we look forward to more memorable matchups and unforgettable games between the Trojans and the Irish."

INDIANA COACH CURT CIGNETTI BECOMES UNSTOPPABLE THANKS TO LATEST DEVELOPMENT ON RECRUITING TRAIL

The first game in the renewed rivalry will be played in Week 1 of the 2030 season at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, with the following season's game also set for Week 1 in South Bend. The games in 2032 and 2033 will both be in the first three weeks of the year, with the option to pick Week 1, 2, or 3.

Riley spoke to the media briefly about the rescheduled announcement.

"We're part of a conference. You know, we have a conference schedule to answer them to. We don't choose our own kickoff times," he said. "I just wanted it to make sense for our team in terms of playing the rest of the Big Ten and Big Ten team travel. And again, we just don't have the same flexibility in our schedule. It is what it is."

This outcome highlighted what was always obvious: the Irish need USC more than the other way around. Notre Dame's schedule this year is, well, not remotely comparable to most teams in the SEC and Big Ten. The Trojans, for example, play Oregon, Ohio State, Indiana, Washington and at Penn State. Indiana being the defending champions, but Oregon and Ohio state being arguably the two best teams heading into 2026. Along with a Penn State road trip, a tough home game against a top-25 level Huskies team, the UCLA rivalry game, and a road game at Wisconsin.

Notre Dame opens with a neutral-site game against Wisconsin, then hosts Rice and Michigan State before road games at Purdue and North Carolina. The Irish return home to face Stanford, travel to BYU, meet Navy at a neutral site, host Miami, Boston College and SMU, then close the regular season at Syracuse. Oh, and should they have a good season, as they hope, they won't face Ohio State, Oregon, or Indiana in a conference championship game. They'll simply coast into the playoff.

Without the rigors of a conference schedule to boost their resume, the Irish need USC to provide a game they can point to with the selection committee. Particularly if other schools move towards easier non-conference schedules. As coaches like Steve Sarkisian and Curt Cignetti have either tacitly or openly acknowledged.

Regardless of the motivations, it's a good thing for college football that Notre Dame-USC is back on the schedule. The more exciting non-conference games we can get, the better. As Nick Saban said recently, play 12 games against Power 4 teams and let the chips fall where they may.

item.title: WNBA silent after Caitlin Clark says leagues should determine who should be included in women's sports
item.description: The WNBA CBA states only women can play, but the league won't define the term or explain how eligibility is determined for transgender athletes.
item.content:encoded:
"Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

Sounds simple, right?

That’s the exact language included in the recently signed collective bargaining agreement between the WNBA and the Women’s National Basketball Players Association.

WNBA COACH SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

But there’s one problem: The CBA doesn’t actually define "woman."

That should be easy to resolve, and OutKick/Fox News Digital attempted to do just that. In essence, we asked both the league and the players association: What is a woman?

We did not hear back from either.

The question became particularly relevant after Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark was asked Sunday about the controversy surrounding teammate Sophie Cunningham’s comments that girls and women should not have to compete against biological men.

RILEY GAINES SAYS TARGET CENTER STAFFER TRIED TO SHUT DOWN HER SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SIGN

"I think it’s for leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions," Clark said following Indiana’s 108-100 loss to the Minnesota Lynx. "Our focus is on basketball. That’s what we talk about and how we can get wins and obviously we didn’t do that tonight. So, we need to find an area to improve in that way."

Clark, the biggest star in women's sports, identified who she believes is responsible for resolving the issue: the leagues and governing bodies that operate women’s sports.

So, OutKick/Fox News Digital asked the WNBA and the WNBPA to do exactly what Clark suggested and explain the league’s eligibility standard.

Article XIII, Section 1(a) of the 409-page CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

The document does not define "woman" or "women." The terms "transgender" and "gender identity" do not appear in the agreement.

The CBA contains detailed definitions for dozens of terms, including "rookie," "veteran," "player contract," "team," "regular season" and "WNBA competitions."

But it does not define the word that determines who is eligible to play in the league.

OutKick/Fox News Digital contacted the WNBA and asked five questions:

The WNBA did not respond by Monday's 3 p.m. ET deadline.

OutKick/Fox News Digital also contacted the WNBPA and asked five similar questions:

The WNBPA also did not respond by Monday's 3 p.m. ET deadline.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

That leaves the WNBA in a strange position.

Its governing labor agreement declares that only women may play in the league, but neither the agreement nor the two organizations that negotiated it will explain what that requirement means.

The league has not publicly said whether eligibility is determined by biological sex, gender identity or some other standard. It has not identified who would make that decision, what criteria would be applied or whether a separate transgender-player policy exists outside the CBA.

The agreement also provides no stated process for enforcing the requirement. It does not establish an eligibility-verification procedure, identify what records or information a player must provide, expressly authorize sex or hormone testing for that purpose or explain how the league would resolve a challenge to a player’s eligibility.

Although the CBA requires players to undergo physical examinations and drug testing, those provisions address health, fitness and prohibited substances—not whether a player qualifies as a "woman" under Article XIII. Without a definition or a verification process, it is unclear how the WNBA could determine whether its own eligibility rule had been violated.

Sophie Cunningham made her position clear.

Caitlin Clark said the league and its athletes should find a solution.

The WNBA and its players' association, at least for now, won’t even define the issue.

The WNBA has a rule.

It just won’t say what the rule means.

item.title: Rosie O'Donnell reveals she will return to 'The View' for anniversary, details tension with Whoopi Goldberg
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell revealed a tense moment with Whoopi Goldberg that kept her away from "The View" as she confirmed her return for the 30th anniversary next season.
item.content:encoded:
Rosie O'Donnell revealed Monday that she plans to return to "The View" for its 30th anniversary season during a podcast interview and explained why she hasn't appeared much since exiting her co-host position.

During an interview on "The Tangle" podcast with host Kyle Ridley, the former co-host of the liberal talk show was asked if "The View" had asked her to be a guest on the show.

O'Donnell detailed a tense moment she had with co-host and moderator Whoopi Goldberg the last time she was on the show.

"They've asked me before, but you know, when I was there last, I had sort of a tense time with Whoopi," she said. "I admire her EGOT status, I have respect for her, and I expected that we would be like, you know, Scottie Pippen and Michael Jordan passing the ball back and forth and then shooting, and, you know, leading the team to victory. But that's not exactly what happened."

ROSIE O'DONNELL OPEN TO RETURNING TO 'THE VIEW,' LAMENTS 'THEY HAVEN'T ASKED ME'

"And I think maybe she felt encroached upon in some way, and I was not trying to encroach," O'Donnell continued. "I was just doing it the way that I knew how to do it, and it didn't go so well."

O'Donnell said the two have moved past the tension but that she didn't want to go back on and make it awkward.

"She's a woman who supports women, as am I," she said. "And so, I will go on the 30th anniversary this year and be on in whatever way they want me — just as a guest, you know. They're bringing back all the hosts, I think, for the 30th season. And, you know, I'm pretty proud of that show, what it's become, and how it really speaks to the people and to politics."

She told Ridley she had wanted her and Goldberg to be best friends.

"Well, I wanted us to be best friends, too, to tell you the truth," O'Donnell said. "I went to her house before I went on it, and we had a lovely lunch and talked about everything. And I was like, 'I'm here for you.' And, you know, I thought I was going in safe and sound. And it didn't turn out that way from day one. I made the mistake of throwing to a commercial when she was still talking."

ROSIE O'DONNELL CLAIMS TRUMP HAS 'PTSD RESPONSE' TO HER AS BACKLASH ERUPTS

O'Donnell said one of the show's employees was gesturing for a commercial break, and so she broke for one while Goldberg was still speaking. O'Donnell said Goldberg was "very upset" at the time.

The ABC talk show did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

"The hard-left Trump-loathing audience of 'The View' would clearly love a little Rosie reunion, despite her massive ego creating tensions on the set," Media Research Center (MRC) director of media analysis Tim Graham told Fox News Digital in a statement. "You have to laugh when she compares herself and Whoopi Goldberg to Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen, like they are the world champions of political hot takes." 

"This show is a feminist fever swamp that specializes in conspiracy theories and misinformation. It's not a 'bona fide news program' in any way," Graham added. 

"The View" is currently facing an FCC investigation over its alleged failure to provide equal treatment for political candidates. ABC has asserted that the FCC previously recognized "The View" as a "bona fide" news program in 2002, making it an exception to equal time rules.

CONSERVATIVE WATCHDOG TELLS FCC THAT 'THE VIEW' IS A DEMOCRATIC PARTY OPERATION, NOT A NEWS PROGRAM

The Disney-owned network filed new comments in early July on a petition it initially sent to the FCC in May to have the show be declared a "bona fide" news program. In the months since, the petition has garnered over 77,000 comments defending the show out of concern for government interference.

"The commenters are right to be concerned," the network said. "The First Amendment does not permit the government to sit in an editor’s chair. Yet that is the seat the Commission now proposes to take — deciding which broadcast programs qualify as legitimate news and, for those it finds wanting, compelling them to surrender their airtime to guests they never chose to feature."

ABC also asserted that the FCC recognized "The View" as a "bona fide" news program in 2002 and that the agency's animosity toward the show is due to President Donald Trump.

item.title: Trump DOJ unleashes largest denaturalization effort in department history — and says it’s ‘only the beginning’
item.description: The DOJ filed complaints against 24 naturalized citizens from 17 countries, alleging crimes from attempted murder to marriage fraud in a record surge.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The Department of Justice is moving to revoke the citizenship of 24 individuals who the DOJ said committed crimes ranging from attempted murder to child sexual abuse to identity fraud, marking its largest citizenship revocation surge on record, Fox News Digital learned Monday.

"U.S. citizenship is one of our nation's highest privileges, and it must be obtained lawfully and honestly," Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche told Fox News Digital on Monday. 

"The complaints announced today allege that these individuals secured naturalization through fraud, concealment, or other unlawful conduct— including by concealing violent crimes, sexual offenses against children, fraudulent identities, and other disqualifying facts," said Blanche.

The complaints against the 24 individuals, filed between July 20 and Aug. 3, involve naturalized U.S. citizens who are natives of 17 countries: Pakistan, Moldova, India, Mexico, Colombia, Nigeria, Liberia, Ghana, Jamaica, Taiwan, Honduras, Cameroon, Jordan, Cuba, El Salvador, Haiti and Sweden, Fox News Digital learned. 

DOJ MOVES TO STRIP CITIZENSHIP FROM 17 PEOPLE ACCUSED OF HIDING DISTURBING CRIMES

"Today's filings represent the largest coordinated denaturalization effort in Department history, but they are only the beginning. The Justice Department will continue to use every tool available to protect the integrity of the naturalization process and the safety of the American people," Blanche added.

The cases bring the department's total denaturalization filings to 88 since Jan. 20, 2025, as the Trump administration ramps up efforts to strip citizenship from individuals it says obtained it unlawfully.

The cases span a wide range of alleged conduct that the Justice Department says should have disqualified the individuals from obtaining or keeping U.S. citizenship.

The complaints involve allegations including attempted murder, child sexual abuse, domestic violence, marriage fraud, identity fraud, passport fraud, bank and credit card fraud, and practicing medicine without a license, among other offenses.

"Today marks the largest denaturalization surge in recorded history," said Justice Department’s Civil Division Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD

"Every one of these individuals committed crimes incompatible with U.S. citizenship. We are moving at record speed to denaturalize those who sought to deceive the federal government and abuse the naturalization process."

In one case, the department seeks to denaturalize a man in North Carolina convicted of attempted first-degree murder and assault with a deadly weapon after obtaining citizenship through military service but allegedly failing to meet the required period of honorable service.

ICE NABS ILLEGAL ALIENS CONVICTED OF CHILD SEX CRIMES AND METH TRAFFICKING IN NATIONWIDE ENFORCEMENT SWEEP

Prosecutors also allege a naturalized citizen in South Carolina concealed a violent assault in which he beat and choked his wife, later pleading guilty to assault and battery after the attack left her hospitalized.

In June, DOJ revoked 17 individuals from 13 different countries over allegations of child sexual abuse, narcotics trafficking and large-scale financial fraud.

item.title: Red Sox land three-time All-Star Adley Rutschman, swoop in ahead of Yankees to reach deal with Orioles: report

item.content:encoded:
Look away, New York Yankees fans. The Boston Red Sox have swooped in and nabbed an All-Star catcher on many wish lists before the MLB trade deadline on Monday.

Three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman is heading to Beantown, as the Red Sox and Baltimore Orioles are finalizing a trade before the 6 p.m. deadline, according to multiple reports.

The Red Sox are surging, revitalizing their entire 2026 season from mediocrity to find themselves in an American League Wild Card position at the moment, while only five games back of the AL East lead. They trail the division-leading Tampa Bay Rays, and are not far behind the Yankees.

While players up and down the Red Sox lineup have been hot, Rutschman only adds to that offensive firepower. And the Red Sox definitely believe he can do that because they were willing to get rid of right-hander Anthony Eyanson, their No. 2 prospect per MLB Pipeline, as part of the trade, per ESPN's Jeff Passan.

Rutschman also holds another year of team control for the 2027 MLB season before he is set for free agency the following year.

RED SOX COME BACK FROM THE DEAD, MOVE INTO POSTSEASON CONTENTION WITH REMARKABLE 14-GAME WIN STREAK

The Orioles were already selling their tradable pieces before the deadline, with starter Dean Kreamer and outfielder Taylor Ward both dealt prior to Rutschman. Baltimore hasn’t had the same luck as the Red Sox, owning a 54-58 record and wishing to go in a different direction moving forward.

But Rutschman has been a good piece for them this season, earning his third All-Star nod as he slashes .251/.331/.433 with a .764 OPS, eight homers and 47 RBI across 67 games this season.

Rutschman is a switch-hitter, creating what should be a middle-of-the-order bat for Boston that can do damage on a playoff-hungry squad.

Behind the plate, Rutschman established himself as one of the best catchers in Major League Baseball. With a pitching staff that boasts some of the best arms in the league, Rutschman should be able to slot right in and take over the majority of the duties there.

However, it isn’t expected that Rutschman can carry a full catcher’s workload anymore, so the Red Sox will have to decide between Connor Wong or Carlos Narvaez in those moments to back him up.

And the Yankees can’t be happy that a player like Rutschman will now be playing for their rival, especially considering their catching woes this season. It's no secret the Yankees have been in the market for a catcher, with Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez and J.C. Escarra not producing up to expectations this season.

But with Rutschman headed to the Red Sox and the Miami Marlins sending Liam Hicks to the Rays, the pickings are slim as the deadline approaches.

But the Red Sox couldn’t care less about the Yankees, as they’re riding high after sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers, who angered many when they landed back-to-back AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in a trade with the Detroit Tigers that adds yet another superstar to its comically stacked depth chart.

When the dispatcher asks whether the child is inside the vehicle, the mother replies, "Yes, my 2-year-old daughter was in the backseat. I was dropping off an Instacart order and I came back outside and my car is gone. My daughter was inside."

HELICOPTER FOOTAGE CAPTURES FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY ABANDONING CHILD DURING HIGH-SPEED CHASE FROM DEPUTIES

Moments later, she cries out again, "My daughter was inside!"

The ordeal unfolded around 4:36 p.m. on July 30, according to the Atlanta Police Department.

Police said the vehicle had been left running with the toddler inside while her mother delivered an Instacart order.

LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS ARE TRACKING DRIVERS EVERYWHERE

Officers with the department's Auto Crimes Enforcement Unit immediately began searching for the vehicle and used the city's license plate readers to locate the car, the suspect and the child in under 15 minutes, according to police.

Body camera video released by the department shows officers surrounding the stolen vehicle and ordering the driver to raise his hands and get out.

"Hands up! Hands up!" an officer shouts.

MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD'

"Hands on the window now," another officer orders. "What you're gonna do is you're going to get out and face away from me, you understand me? Get out the car, slow. Put your hands behind your back."

The video shows officers taking the suspect into custody as the toddler cries nearby and her mother works to calm her.

"It's okay, baby. It's okay, baby," the mother can be heard saying.

Moments later, an officer radios, "The child is okay. The child's okay."

Police identified the suspect as 21-year-old Saleem Martin.

Martin was charged with kidnapping, theft by taking, simple battery, entering an automobile, cruelty to children and criminal attempt to commit a felony, according to police.

Authorities said the toddler was unharmed and reunited with her parents.

According to an arrest warrant obtained by Atlanta NBC affiliate 11Alive, the child's mother later noticed that the bottom of her daughter's dress was unbuttoned.

The warrant alleges the toddler told her mother "the man did it," referring to the man who had been driving the car.

Martin allegedly had both hands on the child's torso when officers found him and was trying to duck down and hide between the seats, according to the warrant cited by the outlet.

The Atlanta Police Department's Special Victims Unit was brought into the investigation.

Martin allegedly told investigators he had been touching the child because he was trying to calm her down, according to 11Alive.

He also allegedly claimed he jumped into the vehicle because he was trying to "get back to New Jersey" and did not realize the toddler was in the backseat until after he drove away.

According to the arrest warrant, Martin also allegedly told investigators he realized there was an iPad inside the vehicle and discarded it because he believed it could be used to track him.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Atlanta Police Department for comment.

item.title: Nick Saban's assistants had a system for sneaking onto golf courses without him knowing, until it backfired
item.description: Steve Sarkisian drained a hole-in-one while hiding from Nick Saban on a Tuscaloosa golf course during spring practice, and word traveled fast.
item.content:encoded:
No matter where his assistant coaches went while at Alabama, former coach Nick Saban always had a watchful eye on his staff members who would sneak out of the office for a round of golf.

In Tuscaloosa, there were plenty of interesting stories to come out regarding Saban assistants finding time to get out of the office in the offseason.

College football is finally back after months of NCAA lawsuits, NIL drama and congressional fights

Whether it was scrambling to get a round of basketball in during their 'free time' or trying to decipher which golf course within driving range of Alabama's campus that Nick Saban was heading to for a round was all part of the game.

For Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, there was a method to their madness, and it involved getting a tip from whomever Saban was golfing with that day.

Whichever course Saban went to, the assistants would head to the other one in town. That worked, until the now Rebels coach had a breakdown in communication on where their boss was actually at.

"There are two courses in Tuscaloosa. You got Indian Hills and you got North River," Pete Golding explained. "I was told that coach Saban was playing North River. So, I got our group together and said 'hey, let's go to to Indian Hills' during the day at like 2 o'clock. Sometimes in the spring after lunch, coach (Saban) would disappear. You wouldn’t know, he didn’t tell ya.

LANE KIFFIN CAN'T STOP TALKING ABOUT OLE MISS, EVEN WHILE EXPLAINING WHY HE CHOSE LSU OVER FLORIDA

"Well, we're on 10, which is a Par-3 over the water and sixteen is coming back in this direction. We got Stoops, Sarkisian and Freddie Roach. So, Sark is about to tee-off and we look down on sixteen green, and there's coach Saban with the Pro at Indian Hills and two of his buddies."

Ok, well right then Golding had to know the jig was up.

The Alabama assistant coach and his co-workers should have probably called it a day. But, given that they were already on the course, and their boss was down the fairway on another hole, the foursome decided to risk it.

Unfortunately, this would turn out to be one of the craziest experiences for the assistant coaches, thanks to a shot from now Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian.

"We're deciding should we hit or not, and Sark is like we'll just be quiet and hit," Golding recalled. "He hits like 145 or whatever, with an eight-iron. He hits it, then it hits like one time and goes in the hole. A hole-in-one. It's like you're watching a movie in mute. Nobody wants to say anything, because we can't let Saban know.

"The pro over there sees it and asks 'who hit that'. We bee-lined straight for the carts, like nobody else even hits and we're down there hiding in the woods or whatever."

In case you were wondering, it did not take long for coach Nick Saban to find out about the insane hole-in-one from his assistant coach, Steve Sarkisian. If you've never been to Tuscaloosa, I promise you that word travels fast, especially on the golf course.

"We hear about it the next day. He ain't gonna sit around and come over there and make it awkward."

Imagine that. Hitting a fantastic shot, knowing that the strictest coach in college football is standing just over on the next green, and you cannot celebrate the shot.

This actually makes the entire afternoon that much better, at least in my eyes.

Nick Saban is known for being a competitor on the course, so figuring out that Steve Sarkisian drained a hole-in-one while the staff was supposed to be back at the office breaking down film during the spring undoubtedly had the former Alabama coach looking for answers.

And, it wouldn’t take him long to find out who hit the shot.

I think we've all heard the stories of what it was like working for Nick Saban as an assistant coach at any one of his stops as a head coach.

But, deciding to still move forward with their round of golf knowing the boss would find out at some point took fortitude.

Now, imagine the other stories that could be told from Saban's time at Alabama.

item.title: Michigan's Democratic AG refuses to attend upcoming convention over harassment concerns
item.description: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel said she won't attend the Michigan Democratic Party convention in August, citing fears of harassment and antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel told Jewish leaders and community members during a roundtable last week that she has no plans to attend the Michigan Democratic Party’s nominating convention next month out of concern for her safety.

"I feel like my presence isn’t going to be welcome," Nessel said, according to the Michigan Advance. "I don’t want to get chased around. I don’t want to get harassed. I don’t want to get yelled and screamed at. I don’t want to get booed off the stage, irrespective of what I’m saying. And I believe that if I go, that is what will happen because it’s been happening to me."

Nessel, the first Jewish person to be elected Michigan's attorney general, claimed that party leadership has neglected her concerns over the rise of antisemitism within the Democratic Party despite reporting that she was harassed by some members.

Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus chair Jessica Alexander told Fox News Digital that she respected Nessel's decision and, though she does not believe that the Democratic Party itself is antisemitic, acknowledged a rise in "anti-Jewish" attitudes among dissenters. 

LEFT-WING ACTIVISTS HECKLE PRO-ISRAEL DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS AT MICHIGAN CONVENTION

"At this point, why should she put herself in a circumstance that feels untenable and reactionary? As active and dedicated members, we don't feel or believe the Democratic Party is antisemitic, but the anti-AIPAC rhetoric circling many current campaigns is a dog whistle for classic anti-Jewish tropes such as ‘Jews hold the power, they have the money, rising gas prices are their fault, etc.,’" Alexander said.

Alexander, who is a professor at Eastern Michigan University, added that as someone not "open to immense scrutiny" like an elected official, she is planning on attending the convention, expecting a "large turnout" for her caucus. 

Nessel said she could say as a Democrat that "some things have changed," according to the Advance, and that society had to exist where "intelligent discourse and debate" could occur without threats.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Michigan Democratic Party for comment.

BILL MAHER OFFERS A STARK WARNING FOR DEMOCRATS CODDLING ANTISEMITES, CALLS OUT ‘WOKE IDIOTS’ IN THE PARTY

A spokesperson for the Michigan Democratic Party told the Michigan Advance that the party rejects "antisemitism, Islamophobia, and all forms of hateful conduct" and that the organization is "ensuring party-hosted events are safe and secure environments for all attendees" at the Aug. 29 convention.

Nessel revealed in 2023 that she was the target of a "heavily armed defendant" who was allegedly plotting attacks against Jewish elected officials in the wake of Israel's war in Gaza.

She also clashed with progressive "Squad" member Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., after bringing charges against anti-Israel protesters at the University of Michigan.

BATYA UNGAR-SARGON EXPLAINS WHY SO MANY AMERICAN JEWS BECAME DEMS — AND WHY SOME NOW FEEL POLITICALLY HOMELESS

Nessel is far from the only Michigan Democrat to express concerns over antisemitism within her party. Former Senate candidate Mallory McMorrow confirmed during a debate in May before she suspended her campaign that disdain for Jewish people among Democrats is a growing problem.

"At the Democratic convention, an attendee yelled an antisemitic slur at my husband, who is Jewish and was walking with my 5-year-old daughter. That is terrifying," McMorrow said.

Some Jewish Democrats have also reported intending to vote for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers if progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed wins the upcoming Democratic primary.

item.title: Maggie Sajak is ashamed of her Dodgers, baseball player throws a punch during a pickle & ESPN's trans drooling
item.description: Tarik Skubal's trade to the Dodgers has fans fuming and demanding a salary cap as the MLB trade deadline fuels serious lockout fears this winter.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy MLB Trade Deadline day to all who celebrate!

Sure, I know that's a niche topic, but man — there is nothing better than a trade deadline day in sports. Any sport, really. Take your pick.

The NFL trade deadline in October used to be a waste of time, but not anymore. The baseball deadline has always been electric, and this year is no different.

In fact, people are on edge from coast to coast right now because of the Tarik Skubal trade over the weekend. Did you hear about that?

SENDING ACE PITCHER TARIK SKUBAL TO THE LOS ANGELES DODGERS WOULD OFFICIALLY RUIN BASEBALL

Of course you did! Fans are FUMING right now. Folks are ready to lock it down. They want a salary cap. They want the Dodgers relegated forever. Even LA fans are walking on eggshells.

Speaking of ... welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Maggie Sajak bleeds Dodger blue in secrecy as baseball barrels towards a lost season. We'll get into it.

What else? I've got a Mexican League player sucker punching a third baseman during a rundown (seriously), ESPN Radio bringing back Mike Golic out of nowhere, and how about the insane gushing by the World Wide (Woke) Leader over the Minnesota coach yesterday?

My God. These people are just nuts. It's amazing.

OK, grab you a chocolate chip cookie for National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

My wife made some sort of healthy, chickpea/almond flour/protein powder chocolate chip cookies today for the kids, and they were good. Fair is fair, and they got the job done. MAHA Mom!

That being said, the healthy stuff doesn't hold a candle to the old school ingredients. Not even close.

Mount Rushmore of Cookies? Sure, why not? It's the first Monday of August, after all.

1. Heath Bar (the ones from Publix deserve to be in the Hall of Fame)

2. Sugar (needs to be soft and a little doughy, though)

3. Peanut Butter (see above)

4. Oatmeal Raisin (probably won't be popular but that doesn't mean it's wrong)

There you have it. You are welcome! Another great Ted Talk in the books to start August.

Now, let's get this class started by checking in with Maggie Sajak and the LA Dodgers, who are officially the most villainous team in sports since ... the '90s Yankees?

Does Maggie speak for all Dodgers fans today? Are you embarrassed by your team?

Look, I'm not Dodger fan. I'm actually a Red Sox fan, which has been just incredible over the past six weeks. 28-5 since June 26! Just amazing.

Anyway, I don't blame the Dodgers. Some folks are furious with them today. Everyone is convinced they're ruining baseball and pushing us towards a lockout this winter.

That may be the case, but the Skubal trade has nothing to do with it. Literally any team in baseball could A) afford to have taken on Skubal's $9 million salary for the rest of this year, and B) put together a package to match what the Dodgers gave up ...

... mainly because it was a pretty crappy package.

So, why were the Dodgers the only team to step up to the plate? Or, better yet, why did the Tigers jump at that trade? I have no clue, but I do have a conspiracy theory.

The rabbit hole in me thinks the rest of the owners allowed the Dodgers to make this trade because they want the public on their side during these upcoming negotiations. They were thinking long term.

These lockouts are always about perception. It dictates everything, and it's usually on the players' side.

This looming lockout — and there will 100% be a lockout — could be the first time in history where the fans side with the owners.

Regardless, don't blame the Dodgers for picking up the phone and making the call. They gave up peanuts for a two-time Cy Young award winner. Every other team could've done it, and they chose not to.

At least the LA faithful packed the stadium yesterday to show their appreciation!

Lordy. Look at that stadium! It was half-empty for a Sunday afternoon game against the Red Sox! Boots on the ground tell me that a bunch of fans didn't show up because it was "hot" and "sunny."

Give me a break. Hilarious.

OK, let's leave LA and head across the border, where Mexican League outfielder Danry Vasquez punched his way out of a pickle this weekend:

Whoaaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! I've been in baseball for a long time now — as a player and now a Big J writer — and I can confidently say that I've never seen someone do that. What a brawl.

And how about the shot Vasquez took after landing the initial punch? Just gets pummeled from behind. Absolute beatdown.

Now, peeling back the curtain a bit here, I'd normally go into a long diatribe breaking this fight down — punch by punch. I'd have some fun with it.

BUT, some digging showed me that this Danry Vasquez is an absolute scumbag and has done some really disgusting things in the past. Yes, there is video. Yes, it involved his girlfriend. No, I will not be showing it here.

You can find it on your own if you'd like, it's not hard. It's a tough watch. I'd suggest you just take my word for it.

Seems like this guy shouldn't ever be allowed near a baseball field again.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night of trading! First up? I can't get over the wokes over at ESPN gushing over the Lynx coach wearing a 'protect trans kids' shirt during yesterday's game:

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TAKES VICIOUS ELBOW TO FACE, AND FANS FUME AT WHAT REFS DID NEXT

"I would encourage to go and listen to Cheryl Reeve's comments."

Yeah, no ... we're good. Thanks, though, ESPN! And how about the stones on Cheryl giving Sophie Cunningham a lecture before the game?

What did Trump say during his SOTU earlier this year?

"These people are CRAZY."

They really are. Just insane.

Speaking of ESPN ... anyone notice who was back on the FM/AM airwaves this morning?

Mike Golic! Wow. What a throwback. I hadn't heard Golic on ESPN in a decade. Lordy, do I miss those days.

I can vividly remember waking up every day at the crack of dawn and going to school in the old 1997 jeep wrangler with the top down and listening to a static "Mike & Mike" on AM radio. It was a staple in our car for years. Then we'd get Cowherd on the drive home.

Perhaps this is the latest sign that ESPN is moving back to that era? I hope so, but I'll believe it when I see it.

After all, we did have an announcer treating Cheryl Reeves wearing a pro-trans shirt like the falling of the Berlin wall just 24 hours ago, so I won't be holding my breath.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Good start to August.

Here's an old broadcast of the night that Yankees great Thurman Munson died to take us into the week.

Incredible scene.

RIP!

Are the Dodgers to blame for the Skubal trade? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

Phil Collins' biggest heartbreak didn't happen onstage.

The music icon revealed the emotional goodbye he shared with his children in 2024 while facing life-threatening health struggles and alcoholism, unsure if he would make it home. Collins' manager called up the singer's five children — Lily, Joely, Simon, Nicolas and Matthew — while he lay unconscious in a Swiss hospital.

"Because there were some decisions to be made about ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’ kind of thing," he told The Sunday Times.

RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY

"My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up," Collins explained. "People were coming to say goodbye."

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

Surviving the ordeal prompted Collins to make a life-changing decision about his drinking.

Months later, Collins spent time reconnecting with his kids after surviving the frightening brush with death. Lily "was sitting beside me in tears, saying, ‘I never thought I’d get these moments,'" he recalled.

He built a Hall of Fame career as both the drummer and later lead singer of Genesis before becoming a global solo superstar in the 1980s.

Collins didn't shy away from describing how quickly his life unraveled after retirement.

"It took me until the age of 55 to become an alcoholic," he wrote. "I got through the heady Sixties, the trippy Seventies, the imperial Eighties, the busy Nineties. I was retired, content – then I fell. Because suddenly, I had too much time on my hands."

item.title: Renewed patriotism and career opportunities fuel Army's biggest recruiting surge in years

The U.S. Army has already reached its fiscal year 2026 active-duty recruiting goal months ahead of schedule, marking a dramatic turnaround after years of falling short as military leaders point to renewed patriotism, career opportunities and a growing sense of purpose among young Americans choosing to serve.

Fox News was granted exclusive access inside Fort Hood, one of the Army’s largest installations, where commanders and soldiers offered a firsthand look at what they say is driving the recruiting resurgence.

Just a few years ago, the Army was struggling to meet its recruiting goals. After hitting a low in fiscal year 2022, recruiting has climbed every year since, rising nearly 38% overall, with the biggest jump coming in fiscal year 2025. "I wanted to do my due diligence and service to my country," Campos told Fox News.

TRUMP GIVES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO FALLEN ARMY LT TYLER FEEHAN AFTER FLYING GRIEVING FAMILY ON AIR FORCE ONE

For Campos, serving in uniform has reinforced both his patriotism and the bonds formed alongside fellow soldiers.

"We serve and protect the United States Constitution and its people from enemies of a foreign and domestic, and we take that to heart."

Jade Root, Army Recruiting battalion commander, said the recent turnaround reflects a broader desire among young Americans to serve.

"Locally we have seen a strong sense of young men and women who want to serve a purpose much higher than themselves. They understand the opportunities that the Army provides to acquire critical skills and leadership skills that will last them a lifetime," Root told Fox News.

Army leaders say today’s recruits are motivated by a combination of patriotism, benefits and a sense of purpose.

The Army says today’s typical recruit is about 23 years old, and recruiters are spending more time in high schools, on college campuses and in local communities to connect with potential future soldiers.

"I always ask our recruiters, remember they are not just a number, this is someone’s son or daughter," Root said.

Today’s Army also extends far beyond traditional combat roles, offering more than 200 career fields, ranging from medics and helicopter mechanics to cybersecurity, engineering, military intelligence and animal care.

As modern warfare continues to evolve, Army leaders say they’re increasingly looking for recruits with technical skills in areas such as cybersecurity, engineering and military intelligence as the service prepares for the future battlefield.

For commanders at Fort Hood, the recruiting rebound is about more than reaching a numerical goal. They say it reflects a new generation stepping forward to serve, one motivated by patriotism, opportunity and a willingness to answer the call.

item.title: Eagles' Nolan Smith took apology for his 136 MPH driving arrest to team ownership and now makes it public
item.description: Nolan Smith apologized to Howie Roseman and Jeffrey Lurie after his arrest for driving 136 MPH, but his NFL Personal Conduct Policy status is unclear.
item.content:encoded:
Nolan Smith's brush with the law this offseason led the Philadelphia Eagles linebacker on something of an apology tour but while he's in the clear with the team, his status under the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy remains unclear.

Smith was arrested in May after he was stopped by the Twiggs County Sheriff's Office on charges of for allegedly driving his 2026 Lamborghini at 136 MPH in a 70-MPH stretch of Interstate 16 in Twiggs County, Georgia.

(For the record, there is no stretch of I-16 that allows speeds anywhere close to 136 MPH because it has never been mistaken for a non-regulated portion of the Autobahn in Germany.)

BRANDON AIYUK DROVE 104 MPH NEAR LEVI'S STADIUM AND FILMED IT, NOW A WARRANT HAS BEEN ISSUED FOR HIS ARREST

Anyway, the Sheriff's Office posted on Facebook the night of the incident posted on Facebook that "a traffic stop was initiated, and the vehicle pulled over without incident. The driver was cooperative throughout the encounter ... The driver chose to follow deputies back to the Twiggs County Sheriff’s Office, where citations were issued, bond was posted, and the driver was released. No drama. No injuries. Just a very fast car learning a very expensive lesson."

Smith was cited for speeding and reckless driving.

The Eagles didn't love this and Smith said he was sorry.

He took that apology public on Monday when he spoke of the incident for the first time.

"I apologized to the organization and, um, I'll make that apology now, you know?" Smith told reporters on Monday. "I represent the Eagles no matter where I go. You know, Georgia, Florida. It doesn't matter.

"And that's one of the ones that I own up and I apologize for. And it's just like that we make mistakes and it can't happen again, and that's unacceptable."

Smith says he took his apology as high as he possibly could, including club executive vice president and general manager Howie Roseman and even club Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jeffrey Lurie.

"I did apologize to Howie, I did apologize to Mr. Lurie," Smith said. "I can't let my teammates down like that. They hold me to a different accountability on and off the field."

The Eagles obviously accepted Smith's apology as he remains on the roster, is expected to get significant snaps from his linebacker spot, and is tied contractually to the team through the 2027 season.

Smith suggested there was no disciplinary action from the team.

"Nothing came from it," he said.

But there's the matter of the NFL. An arrest typically initiates an NFL investigation related to its Personal Conduct Policy.

Fox News Digital asked the NFL on Monday if such an investigation involving Smith is ongoing or closed, but has yet to get a reply. It is possible the league has decided to let the club decide the discipline, which it already has.
